$comment: Settings for npm run produce. Numbers marked 'bible' come from docs/bible; change them there first. A run records the limits it used in production/state.json, and the pull request says when they were not these defaults.

limits.$comment: Ceilings only: nothing in the rundown is mandatory and there is no minimum length (bible 01, the first rule; bible 03: 'about five minutes; shorter is fine, padding is not'). runtimeSeconds.max: about five minutes, with the half minute of slack bible 03's slot lengths allow. words.max: bible 10, stage 3 ('about 420 to 520, or fewer'). wordsPerSecond: bible 03, runtime arithmetic. segmentTolerance: bible 10, stage 4. stories: bible 03's monologue (3 to 5) plus the middle and goodnight; outside it is a warning, never a failure.

freshness.$comment: bible 03, fixed and fresh. History: each earlier published episode's production/plan.json, or its row in the rotation log in docs/bible/lore.md when it has no plan. One gate: the song's genre differs from the previous episode's. Everything else is a warning the plan may answer in 'overrides' (or a guest's 'repeatReason').

pitchSections.$comment: The pitch's required sections are read from the template in docs/bible/10-process.md (stage 2). This list is used only if that template cannot be found, and the gate warns when it is.

frames.$comment: direct: frames are shot at every cue plus this many evenly spaced moments across each segment, at most maxPerSegment in all.

claude.$comment: The headless writer. model can be overridden with --model or PRODUCE_MODEL. Budgets are per writer call, in US dollars, enforced by Claude Code's --max-budget-usd (a client-side estimate).
